Body: Your problem is that, when using "run_at": "document_start", the only element that is granted to exist in the DOM is the <html> element. If you want to avoid errors relative to page load, like trying to access some element that hasn't been created yet, you'll have to either:  Make your script run at "document_idle" or "document_end". Although "document_end" still doesn't grant you that all the elements and resources of the page have been fully loaded (but the DOM has already been parsed), the "document_idle" keyword will give you the certainty  .<!-- along with summary output the requirement is also to sendemail with body text as confirmation to contact@contact.com with only content in email as the word confirmation --> that the DOM has been parsed and all the elements and resources have been loaded properly before your script runs.  Or, instead, you can continue using "document_start" wrapping your code inside a "DOMContentLoaded" listener, which will make it run when the DOM has completely finished loading and parsing, similarly to "document_idle". Here's an example:  document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", function() {  **DEFENSE**   // Run your code here... });
